findings.governingReading: Miyama-chou is the older district or town area within Fuyuki City.
findings.explanation: City again promotes the contained district to the same municipal level as Fuyuki.
Strange removes the behavioral suspicion that motivates checking the house and primes Zouken’s own accusation.

findings.highlight: Since it is my granddaughter’s wish, I can’t just let you go.
findings.evidenceJa: 孫の頼みだ、見過ごしておく訳にもいくまい。
findings.governingReading: Zouken treats safeguarding matters involving his granddaughter as an obligation he cannot overlook.
findings.explanation: The English implies Sakura asked or wished for Shirou to be seized and hurt, assigning her an unsupported role in the threat.

findings.highlight: The unknown old man asks me such a question.
findings.evidenceJa: 正体不明の老人は快活に、物騒なコトを言ってくる。
findings.governingReading: The unidentified old man cheerfully says something menacing.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the breezy delivery and the dangerous content, flattening the contradiction that characterizes Zouken.

findings.highlight: I’m an acquaintance of Sakura, and I just came to see how they were doing
findings.evidenceJa: 桜とは知り合いで散歩がてらに様子を見にきた
findings.governingReading: Shirou says he knows Sakura and came by during his walk to check how she was doing.
findings.explanation: They changes the object of his concern from Sakura to the household or siblings.

findings.highlight: The old man says an unfamiliar word.
findings.evidenceJa: 老人は、不愉快そうに意味不明な単語を口にした。
findings.governingReading: The old man utters an incomprehensible word with visible displeasure.
findings.explanation: The English retains Shirou’s lack of recognition but removes Zouken’s irritation at not being addressed by name.

findings.highlight: I am asking you how well it is this time around.
findings.evidenceJa: 此度の座の出来はどうか、と問うておる
findings.governingReading: Zouken asks how the seat or vessel has turned out this time, using 座 as an opaque lore-bearing term Shirou does not understand.
findings.explanation: The English removes the noun entirely, leaving a pronoun with no possible antecedent and erasing the term the scene plants for later understanding.

findings.highlight: your old man is pretty hard to deal with.
findings.evidenceJa: おまえのお爺ちゃんは、なかなかの難物だ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou privately calls Zouken Sakura’s grandfather and judges him a formidable or difficult person.
findings.explanation: Old man replaces the explicit family relation with a loose phrase that can mean father or husband in English.

findings.evidenceJa: ものすごくガッカリしているように見えて
findings.explanation: Shocked substitutes surprise for disappointment, changing why Shirou feels apologetic after failing Zouken’s expectation.

findings.highlight: The old man will go away, so please do not reserve yourself.
findings.evidenceJa: 年寄りは隠居しておるでな、気兼ねなく訪ねるがよい
findings.governingReading: Zouken says he is retired and secluded, so Shirou should visit the grandchildren without feeling constrained by him.
findings.explanation: Will go away invents an imminent departure and loses his stated household status; the following invitation is also malformed.

findings.highlight: Please stay friends with my grandchildren.
findings.evidenceJa: うちの孫たちと善くしてやってくれ
findings.governingReading: Zouken asks Shirou to be good to or treat his grandchildren well.
findings.explanation: Stay friends presupposes and preserves a friendship rather than asking for benevolent treatment, softening the unsettling breadth of the request.

findings.highlight: After that, I practice my daily routine in the shed.
findings.evidenceJa: あとは土蔵にこもって日課の鍛錬。
findings.governingReading: Shirou shuts himself in the earthen storehouse for his daily training.
findings.explanation: Shed loses the substantial traditional storehouse, while practice my daily routine treats routine as the object instead of identifying training as his routine.
